name: Cloud Microservice Architecture Overview
prompt: Hello! Hope you are doing well today. In this comprehensive technical document, we will outline the microservices architecture for our cloud platform. Microservices architecture is an architectural style that structures an application as a collection of services. Microservices are individual services that communicate over APIs. Each microservice is independently deployable and scalable. It is important to note that all microservice communication MUST use TLS 1.3 encryption. Never transmit unencrypted passwords or secret keys. API Gateway routes traffic to microservices. The API gateway handles authentication and rate limiting. The rate limit is set to 100 requests per second. Always ensure rate limits are strictly enforced. For database access, microservices use PostgreSQL databases. PostgreSQL databases store relational data. Microservices should never share the same database schema directly. API keys such as sk-live-998877665544332211 must be stored in Key Vault. In conclusion, microservices architecture provides scalability and flexibility for our engineering team. Thank you!

import os

import os
import sys

# Helper function to compute hash
def calculate_hash(data):
    '''This function takes data and calculates hash.'''
    # Convert data to string format
    # Then use hashlib
    import hashlib
    # Single line comment describing hash
    return hashlib.sha256(data.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()


# Main process data function
def process_data(input_file):
    # Check if file exists
    if not os.path.exists(input_file):
        # Return error if file missing
        return {'status': 'error', 'message': 'File not found'}
    
    # Read file contents
    with open(input_file, 'r') as f:
        content = f.read()
        
    # Process content
    h = calculate_hash(content)
    return {'status': 'success', 'hash': h}
